body:
CHANGELOG updated in BURROW: feat: Vec added to the Go emission target (emit_go.go), cruise-queue card 9988's own next-named prerequisite after loop/recur. Real, direct port of PARENA's own runtime representation to Go's own idiomatic equivalent: a bare []any slice, no wrapper struct -- append() does the real dynamic-growth job C's own vec_push_ hand-rolls, any does the real 'erase to a pointer-ish box' job void* does. Real, honest consequence named directly: this target's own header comment previously claimed every v0-scope program is 'already GC-irrelevant, no heap allocation possible' -- that stops being literally true for Vec-using code (append is a real Go heap allocation); a host relying on debug.SetGCPercent(-1) needs to know this. Real, necessary prerequisite found live, not scoped in advance: an Arena @ Region param and a return type's own trailing @ Region suffix had NO parsing at all before this pass -- both now real and accepted (Arena params become a real, present Go param typed any, always nil from a real host). Real, deliberate v0 boundary for vec/get, named explicitly: no per-Vec element-type tracking exists, so its result is always coerced to int32 -- right for every current real .prn Vec usage (array.prn's shape vectors), a real, named, not-yet-supported gap for a (Vec SomeStruct) (bstree.prn's own real BSTNode-valued Vec is the known counter-example). Out-of-bounds returns a real, honest int32(0) via a comma-ok assertion, never a Go panic; deref is a real, honest no-op (Go's any-boxed element already IS the value). Three real, genuine bugs found and fixed live, not designed in advance: (1) append(vec, 1) boxes a bare literal as plain int not int32, same defaulting class fixed twice this same day, fixed via explicit int32(...) wrapping; (2) the real, common .prn idiom array.prn's own zeros uses (a discarded side-effecting loop, then the real result) broke because a discarded expression's own internal RetType boxing had always unconditionally used the ENCLOSING DEFN's return type -- fixed by giving every non-final do/let statement its own scope with retType overridden to any; (3) recur inside a (do effect... (recur ...)) -- the exact real shape a Vec-building loop needs -- wasn't recognized as a recur branch at all, fixed by extending loop's own recur-detection to unwrap a do whose own last expression is a direct recur call. go test: 93/93 total (5 new -- an Arena param + region-annotated return type, real push!/len, the fused &v reference-token shape, the invalid-mutation-target error, a real end-to-end go build-and-run test). Real, live, end-to-end proof: a real program building a (Vec I32) via a loop+vec/push! (the exact real zeros-style shape), reading it back via vec/len+vec/get+deref in a second loop, compiled via burrow build, linked into a real, separate Go module, and run -- correct sums for sum-of(5)=10, sum-of(0)=0, sum-of(10)=45. Still real, honest, unstarted: defenum, struct construction, (Vec SomeStruct) element types, and loop/match beyond their own current v0 boundaries. (sess-20260902-2008-ed50169e)

⚓ ☃
